title: TMSAT is NP-hard
statement: For every machine-code scheme with a total decoder and the property that encoding any machine followed by any number of $1$-bits decodes to that machine, the associated language of encoded machine descriptions, inputs, unary witness-length bounds, and unary time bounds for which some witness causes the decoded machine to halt with output $1$ is NP-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions.
hypotheses_covered: $c$ is a machine-code scheme with a total decoder
Appending any number of $1$-bits to an encoded machine preserves its decoding
replaced: Let $c$ be a machine-representation scheme, assigning to every bit string $\alpha$ a one-work-tape binary Turing machine $M_\alpha$ so that the code of every such machine decodes back to it. Then $\mathrm{TMSAT}_c$ is $\mathrm{NP}$-hard: every language in $\mathrm{NP}$ reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction, where $\mathrm{TMSAT}_c$ is the set of strings $\langle\alpha,\langle x,\langle 1^n,1^t\rangle\rangle\rangle$, where $\langle a,b\rangle$ is the self-delimiting pair encoding and $1^k$ is the word of $k$ ones, such that some $u$ with $|u| = n$ makes $M_\alpha$ halt on $\langle x,u\rangle$ within $t$ steps with output exactly $1$.
